basics.name: Jacob Tutt
basics.label: PhD Candidate | Bayesian Inference | Machine Learning | Distributed GPU Computing
basics.summary: PhD researcher in machine learning and computational statistics at the Cavendish Laboratory and Kavli Institute for Cosmology, University of Cambridge. My research looks at how the latest statistical and probabilistic machine learning methods, combined with distributed, hardware-accelerated computing, can tackle previously intractable inference problems in physics. I apply this primarily to the statistical detection and characterisation of the cosmological 21-cm signal, but am broadly motivated by the challenge of scaling statistical and numerical methods, both algorithmically and computationally, to ever larger datasets, parameter spaces and physical systems.

education.area: Developing scalable probabilistic machine learning and Bayesian inference methods to extract faint signals from noisy, high-dimensional and highly degenerate data in 21-cm cosmology.
courses: Developing physically motivated forward models, spanning astrophysical simulations to computational electromagnetics, and scalable inference methods with rigorous Bayesian uncertainty quantification for 21-cm cosmology
